title: Lesson 5: Building Reusable IP and Productized Offerings
description: The difference between an offer and the intellectual property underneath it, why IP is the asset that compounds, and how to turn a repeatable delivery method into a productized offering the practice owns and can sell again without reinventing the scope.

questions.explanation: The lesson is centered on: The difference between an offer and the intellectual property underneath it, why IP is the asset that compounds, and how to turn a repeatable delivery method into a productized offering the practice owns and can sell again without reinventing the scope.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson’s guidance?
options: Lesson 2 taught you to turn capability into offers, and Lesson 4 taught you to keep the delivery system coherent with standards and review.
This lesson sits between them and answers a question neither one fully asked: what does the practice actually own?
That distinction, between the offer and the IP that produces it, is the difference between a practice that sells its time and a practice that sells an asset it keeps getting better at producing.
The intellectual property underneath it, the method, the templates, the reference architecture, the accumulated lessons, is something the practice owns and can reuse across every sale.
